proposed_widenings.name: triggered_reaction_magic_item_component
proposed_widenings.justification: Magic items can currently compose only passive and activation parts. Staff of the Magi has a major reaction-shaped ability that cannot be expressed as either without lying about timing and trigger semantics.
proposed_widenings.evidence: In addition, you can take a Reaction when another creature casts a spell that targets only you.

proposed_widenings.name: reaction_trigger.targeted_by_spell_self_only
proposed_widenings.justification: Existing reaction triggers only cover named spells or generic spellcasting with components. Spell Absorption keys off an unnamed spell whose targeting restriction is 'targets only you'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: when another creature casts a spell that targets only you

proposed_widenings.name: modify_damage_roll
proposed_widenings.justification: The passive quarterstaff mode grants a bonus to damage rolls made with the item, and the surface has no atom for passive damage-roll modifiers.
proposed_widenings.evidence: grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it

proposed_widenings.name: weapon_filter.specific_item
proposed_widenings.justification: Current weapon scoping only distinguishes melee vs ranged. Staff of the Magi needs bonuses scoped to this held quarterstaff specifically.
proposed_widenings.evidence: can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it

proposed_widenings.name: roll_kind.spell_attack_roll
proposed_widenings.justification: The item separately boosts spell attack rolls while held. The current roll taxonomy cannot target spell attacks without also hitting weapon attacks.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While you hold it, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls.

proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_advantage.source_filter_spell
proposed_widenings.justification: Spell Absorption grants Advantage on saving throws against spells, but current save/advantage riders cannot narrow by the source being a spell.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you have Advantage on saving throws against spells

proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_attunement.class_restriction
proposed_widenings.justification: MagicItemRecord only captures a boolean attunement flag. Staff of the Magi requires attunement by one of a closed class set.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Requires Attunement by a Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard

proposed_widenings.name: area_origin.item_self
proposed_widenings.justification: Retributive Strike's explosion originates from the staff itself, not the wielder, a target, or a point within range.
proposed_widenings.evidence: an explosion that fills a 30-foot Emanation originating from itself

proposed_widenings.name: dice_amount.resource_spent_multiplier
proposed_widenings.justification: Retributive Strike damage is a fixed multiple of the staff's current charges, not simply equal to charges spent.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you take Force damage equal to 16 times the number of charges in the staff ... a creature takes Force damage equal to 6 times the number of charges in the staff

proposed_widenings.name: charge_pool_refund_and_overflow_resolution
proposed_widenings.justification: Spell Absorption adds charges based on absorbed spell level and can overflow into an immediate Retributive Strike-style explosion. The current surface has no honest way to model reactive charge gain plus overflow consequences.
proposed_widenings.evidence: the staff absorbs the magic of the spell, canceling its effect and gaining a number of charges equal to the absorbed spell's level. However, if doing so brings the staff's total number of charges above 50, the staff explodes as if you activated its Retributive Strike

notes: The spell table, charge pool, and dawn recharge mostly fit existing magic-item activation patterns, but the unit as a whole does not fit honestly because it combines passive, triggered-reaction, and activated mechanics, and several supporting filters/atoms are still missing.
